name: Best Project Sequence for Roof, Seismic Retrofit, and Remodel in Los Angeles

mainEntity.name: What sequencing makes sense if I need roof replacement, seismic retrofitting, and interior remodeling on the same Los Angeles home?
mainEntity.text: What sequencing makes sense if I need roof replacement, seismic retrofitting, and interior remodeling on the same Los Angeles home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Homeowners often schedule projects based on available cash or contractor timing, but the order of major work on a Los Angeles home has big cost and risk implications. When you need seismic retrofitting, interior remodeling, and a new roof, sequencing incorrectly can mean opening brand-new finishes or roofs to complete missed work. In most cases, structural and seismic upgrades should come first. Foundation bolting, shear wall installation, and framing changes for new openings or additions often require significant demolition of walls and sometimes roof areas. Completing this work upfront establishes a stable shell. Once the structure is correct, move to interior remodeling: framing non-structural walls, rough plumbing and electrical, insulation, and finishes. During this phase, you will also finalize roof penetrations for new vents, range hoods, bathroom fans, and possibly future solar conduit. Roof replacement should typically be last among these major scopes. Installing the final roofing system after interior and mechanical penetrations are set reduces the need to disturb a new roof and protects your investment. Exterior painting or stucco repairs often follow or overlap with roofing. Work with a general contractor capable of coordinating all scopes so that inspections, trade schedules, and city approvals follow this logical sequence and minimize both downtime and rework.
acceptedAnswer.description: Complete structural and seismic work first, then interior remodeling, and finish with roof replacement and exterior finishes. This sequence minimizes rework, prevents damage to new finishes, and lets structural upgrades, penetrations, and venting be coordinated before installing the final roofing system.
